prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a ubiquitin ligase to a chosen protein and so reprogram cellular proteolysis, from heterobifunctional degraders to the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues

statement.case_for: I have moved from first-principles molecular dynamics (B059) to targeted protein degradation (B054). Reading all eight files, B054 is the one achievement that colleagues reach from different directions: two members prefer it, five more list it as an alternative, and it had the broadest top-three support in the openings. That does not substitute for judgment, so on the science: induced proximity is a new chemical principle that turns a small molecule into a bridge between an E3 ligase and a target, so that the cell's own machinery does the work. It is conceptually simple, it is supported by ternary-complex structures and degradation kinetics, and it meets my own standard of something completely new with demonstrated consequences, since glue-class drugs derived from the cereblon mechanism are already approved and heterobifunctional degraders are in late-stage trials. Brzezinski's argument persuaded me on the third name. Crews and Deshaies supply the concept and its first demonstration, while Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target and so explained how the glue branch works; that is a discovery of mechanism, which I now weigh above the later structure-guided optimisation I favoured in round 1 for Ciulli. One citation covering concept and mechanism is coherent because both rest on the same principle of hijacking ubiquitin ligase specificity.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional degrader is approved, so half of the citation still rests on late-stage trial evidence rather than on a drug. Credit is split across two lineages and at least eight names, and any three-person cut leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim, whose work made the field practical; I accept that this cost is real and not merely rhetorical. A single citation spanning PROTACs and glues could also be criticised as joining two discoveries, which is Chabes's and Somfai's worry. Finally, I give up the cleanest attribution on the list: Car and Parrinello remain an overdue, forty-year-validated pair, and I do not claim B054 is cleaner on credit or more mature in the sense of method validation.

responses.point: Keep the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism in one citation, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, because Handa's identification of cereblon is a more fundamental mechanistic discovery than later ligand optimisation.
responses.response: I now agree, and this is the main reason I changed my configuration. In round 1 I argued for Ciulli as the third name; your point that Handa explained a long-standing pharmacological puzzle, and that the glue branch is where approved drugs exist, answers my own maturity concern better than my original trio did. I still think a citation must be written so that it does not claim more than the evidence shows: concept demonstrated, mechanism established, heterobifunctional clinical benefit still pending. Ciulli and Sakamoto stay outside, and I regard that as an unavoidable cost of the three-person limit rather than a judgement that their work was minor.

responses.point: A two-part prize pairing base editing (Liu) with heterobifunctional degraders (Crews, Deshaies) draws on the broadest opening support and keeps the total at three people.
responses.response: I see the logic, and B069 is my alternative. I prefer a single part for B054 for two reasons. First, the two themes are both chemical biology for medicine and do not form one achievement, as you concede yourself. Second, your pairing leaves out Handa and Ito, which splits the degrader field at exactly the point where the mechanistic discovery lies, while Liu's part omits Komor and Gaudelli and leaves the Target-AID priority question unaddressed. I would rather make one defensible attribution well than two that each need an apology. I am also not persuaded that base editing has shown a new principle beyond the 2020 CRISPR prize that the committee can state in one sentence.

responses.point: With three seats a citation cannot cover both the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito) without leaving out someone decisive.
responses.response: That is the sharpest objection to my configuration and I do not think it can be fully answered. My answer is that the citation should be about the principle, ligase-directed degradation induced by a small molecule, and the three names are chosen as the concept's origin (Crews, Deshaies) and the mechanistic proof that explains the glue class (Handa). Ito and Ciulli are omitted either way, whichever strand is chosen. If the committee decides the strands are separate achievements, I would prefer the broader concept as one part over a narrow cereblon-only prize. I also note that your own first alternative is B054, which suggests we agree on the chemistry and differ only on the cut.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello is a strong alternative, but its discovery would have to be defined narrowly because of the 1998 DFT prize and the overlap with metadynamics and machine-learned potentials; Linke asked what exactly would be cited.
responses.response: This was a fair challenge and I could not answer it to the extent I wanted: the narrow statement, unifying electronic structure and ionic motion in one simulation, is real but is also the part that overlaps most with the 1998 recognition of density functional theory. That, together with the thin support, is why I no longer lead with B059, though it remains my first alternative. On B017 I agree with you on the science and I still hold the reservation that stability and deployment are open; if the committee prefers a materials prize, your trio of Miyasaka, Snaith and Park is the defensible one, and the citation should be anchored on absorber and efficiency, not on devices, to stay clear of the Gratzel and Seok priority dispute.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry of siRNA and mRNA medicines, with clear overwhelming confirmation, and Aili would accept either Ciulli or Handa as the third degrader name if B054 became the prize.
responses.response: I appreciate that flexibility, and it helps: it suggests B054 can be settled on attribution without splitting you from the supporters. On B036, my round-1 difficulty is unchanged. The chemical principle, near-neutral at physiological pH and cationic in the endosome, is clear, but the decisive credit is spread over Vancouver and MIT groups and industrial formulators, and I cannot see a trio that does not leave out Hope, MacLachlan or Madden. That is a reason to keep it as a candidate for a later year, not a judgement on its importance.

uncertainties: Whether five members will accept one citation spanning the heterobifunctional concept and the cereblon mechanism, or insist on treating them as separate achievements.

Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader should delay recognition; I weigh the approved glue drugs and the late-stage trials as sufficient, but I cannot verify trial outcomes from the materials available to me.
The priority and relative contribution of Handa versus Ciulli, Sakamoto and Ito, which I take from colleagues' accounts rather than from primary records.
Whether B059 would attract more support than I credited if the citation were defined narrowly, given that I am setting aside my own first preference.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need. My Warshel collaboration and Uppsala ribosome and RNA connections involve no credited person in B054, and I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Car or Parrinello. My work in simulation is adjacent to B059 only, which I am no longer proposing as my preferred position.
